plain_description.what: Cuts each of three fresh content-closed trees at every depth and compares each cut with a flat k-means clustering that has the same number of cells, by how well cells match the held-out subject labels. No judge calls.
plain_description.why: The tree was only compared with flat clustering at its finest level; a tree's value includes its coarser levels, so each level is checked against a flat fit of the same size.
plain_description.information: Shows whether the tree's coarser levels are worse, equal or better partitions than flat clustering of the same size. Result: done. On all three fresh trees, cutting the tree at a level gives a worse grouping (by subject labels on unseen items) than a flat k-means of the same size, by about 3 points of purity.
